name: Westin Santa Fe Mexico City
positioning: Business district hotel in Santa Fe, Mexico City, with valley views and a Jean-Georges Vongerichten restaurant (officially The Westin Santa Fe, Mexico City)
best_for: Business travelers attending events at the Santa Fe Convention Center
Families or groups wanting two-bedroom suites

facts.text: The hotel is in the heart of Santa Fe's Financial District, with access to the Santa Fe Convention Center and Centro Santa Fe.
Rooms have modern furnishings in warm wood tones and marble bathrooms with a rain shower.
Rooms are large and airy, with spare, modern furnishings.
Eleven Bar & Lounge has an outdoor rooftop terrace.
The Heavenly Spa by Westin has seven treatment cabins.
The gym has TechnoGym equipment and natural light.
Two-bedroom suites suit group and family stays.
The concierge helps with recommendations, tickets and transportation for cultural tours in and around the city.

highlights.text: The Presidential Suite has floor-to-ceiling windows with views of the city and the valley's green reserves.
The hotel has striking valley views despite its business district location.
Market Kitchen was created by French chef Jean-Georges Vongerichten with a farm-to-table concept.
Bathrooms are decorated in Greek Spider Gold marble.
Club Level Suites include Club Lounge access with snacks, drinks and preferred service.

considerations.text: In the Santa Fe business district, modern high-rises contrast with the traditional Mexican architecture found elsewhere in the city.
WhataHotel notes the business district location may feel less cultural for leisure travelers.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing typical of international hotel chains.
